front: Which annotation injects a constructor, field, or setter dependency in Spring?
hint: Constructor injection can omit it entirely when there is a single constructor.

front: Which annotation binds an HTTP request body to a method parameter as a Java object?
hint: Spring uses an HttpMessageConverter, such as Jackson, to deserialize it.

front: Which annotation maps a query string parameter to a method parameter?
hint: It can declare a default value and whether the parameter is required.

front: What is the difference between @Controller and @RestController?
back: @RestController combines @Controller with @ResponseBody, so every handler method's return value is written directly to the response body, typically as JSON, instead of being resolved as a view name.
accepted_answers: @RestController adds @ResponseBody so return values become the response body instead of a view name
hint: @Controller alone is meant for server-rendered views.

front: What is the difference between @Component, @Service, and @Repository?
back: All three register a class as a Spring bean; @Service and @Repository are specializations of @Component that document intent, and @Repository additionally translates persistence-specific exceptions into Spring's DataAccessException hierarchy.
accepted_answers: all register beans; @Repository also translates persistence exceptions into DataAccessException
hint: @Repository's exception translation is the one functional difference beyond documentation.

front: Why does Spring Boot's default singleton bean scope matter for storing per-request mutable state in a @Service class?
back: A singleton bean is created once and shared by every request, so storing per-request mutable state as instance fields causes data from concurrent requests to interfere with each other; per-request data should stay in method parameters, local variables, or request-scoped beans.
accepted_answers: singleton beans are shared across all requests so per-request mutable instance state causes cross-request interference
hint: Thread safety of a singleton service depends entirely on avoiding shared mutable instance state.

front: What is the purpose of a DTO layer between REST controllers and JPA entities?
back: A DTO decouples the API's request and response shape from the persistence model, letting the entity evolve independently, hiding internal fields, and avoiding accidental serialization of lazy-loaded associations.
accepted_answers: decouples the API shape from the entity and avoids exposing internal or lazy fields
hint: Serializing an entity directly risks leaking fields or triggering lazy-loading errors.

front: Why does Spring MVC choose between multiple @GetMapping handlers based on their path and parameter specificity rather than declaration order?
back: Spring's request mapping resolves the most specific matching handler for a request's path, HTTP method, headers, and parameters, since request dispatch is driven by declared matching criteria, not by the order methods appear in the class.
accepted_answers: dispatch is based on declared matching criteria not declaration order
hint: Ambiguous mappings that are equally specific throw an exception at startup instead of silently picking one.

front: A @GetMapping("/users/{id}") handler returns a User object directly instead of a ResponseEntity, and the object is found. What HTTP status code does Spring Boot return by default?
hint: Returning the object directly, not a ResponseEntity, uses the default success status.

front: A @PostMapping handler returns ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CREATED).body(saved);. What HTTP status code is sent to the client?
hint: HttpStatus.CREATED corresponds to 201.

front: A client sends a request body that is missing a field marked @NotNull and validated with @Valid on a @RequestBody parameter. What HTTP status is returned by default when no custom exception handler exists?
hint: Bean validation failures on @Valid @RequestBody trigger a client-error response by default.

front: A controller parameter is annotated @RequestParam("page") int page, but the client omits the page query parameter entirely and no default value is set. What happens when the request is handled?
back: Spring throws a MissingServletRequestParameterException, which by default results in a 400 Bad Request response, because the parameter is required unless a default value or required = false is set.
accepted_answers: a MissingServletRequestParameterException resulting in 400 Bad Request
hint: @RequestParam parameters are required unless declared otherwise.

front: A REST client receives a 500 error with a stack trace exposing internal package names for what should be a simple not-found case. What is the recommended fix?
back: Add a centralized exception handler, such as @ControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler, that catches the not-found condition and returns a clean 404 response instead of letting an unhandled exception leak internal details through the default error page.
accepted_answers: add a @ControllerAdvice exception handler that maps the condition to a clean 404
hint: Unhandled exceptions in Spring MVC surface as a generic 500 with stack trace details by default.

front: Two @GetMapping methods in the same controller both map to GET /items with no distinguishing parameters or headers, and the application fails to start. What is the cause?
back: Spring detects an ambiguous mapping between two handlers matching the identical route and method with no further distinguishing criteria, and fails fast at startup instead of guessing which one should handle the request.
accepted_answers: an ambiguous mapping between two handlers for the identical route causes a startup failure
hint: This is a startup-time failure, not a runtime dispatch choice.

front: A @Autowired field of an interface type fails to start the application with "expected single matching bean but found 2". What are the two typical fixes?
back: Either mark one implementation as the default with @Primary, or disambiguate the injection point with @Qualifier naming the specific bean, since Spring cannot choose between two equally eligible implementations on its own.
accepted_answers: use @Primary on one bean or @Qualifier at the injection point to disambiguate
hint: @Primary sets a default; @Qualifier is explicit at each injection site.

front: A REST endpoint that used to return JSON now returns 406 Not Acceptable for the same client request after a library upgrade removed a Jackson dependency. What is the most likely cause?
back: Spring Boot could no longer find an HttpMessageConverter capable of producing the client's requested application/json type because the Jackson library that provided JSON conversion was removed, so content negotiation fails with 406.
accepted_answers: no HttpMessageConverter could produce JSON because the Jackson dependency was removed
hint: 406 means the server could not produce a representation matching the Accept header.

front: A controller endpoint deserializes untrusted @RequestBody JSON directly into a JPA entity and saves it, and a client is able to set an internal field, like a role flag, that the UI never exposes. What is the underlying vulnerability and fix?
back: This is a mass assignment vulnerability: binding attacker-controlled JSON directly onto a persistence entity lets the client set fields it should never control; the fix is to bind requests to a dedicated DTO that only exposes the fields the client is allowed to set.
accepted_answers: mass assignment from binding request JSON directly onto the entity; fix by using a DTO with only allowed fields
hint: The entity's full field surface should never be the same as the API's writable surface.

front: Write a Spring MVC exception handler method inside a @ControllerAdvice class that returns a 404 ResponseEntity<String> with body "Not found" when a NoSuchElementException is thrown.
back: @ExceptionHandler(NoSuchElementException.class) public ResponseEntity<String> handleNotFound(NoSuchElementException ex) { return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND).body("Not found"); }
accepted_answers: @ExceptionHandler(NoSuchElementException.class) public ResponseEntity<String> handleNotFound(NoSuchElementException ex) { return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND).body("Not found"); }
hint: @ExceptionHandler declares which exception type the method handles.

hint: The path variable name in braces should match the parameter name or be specified explicitly.
